{"self_assessment": "Impact: I got the build moving early. I fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin at the start, so nobody ran short while the lines went up. I laid the start domino at the nose and built the top line of the fish from it, which everything else grows from. When the bottom tail needed work, I volunteered for it so the table wasn't waiting. By our final check, the run traced as connected from the start through all 127 standing dominoes.

Execution: I worked the plan in order: start domino, then stroke one, then the bottom tail join. I made several close inspections of the nose, the bottom join and the tail region to confirm the chain was connected. I stood a fallen domino back up when I found one. I kept my hands off the table once the run was connected, which cut the risk of a bump before the push.

Collaboration: I agreed early on the split of top line and bottom line and said so clearly. I told the table what I was taking on, so we didn't double up on work or crowd each other's hands. I reported what I saw from my close looks at the joins, and I backed the team's decision to leave the table alone before the push.

Leadership: I took the stroke that lays the start, which was the critical dependency, and I committed to it out loud. I moved onto the bottom tail without being asked so the work didn't stall. In the final minutes I helped keep the group calm and settled on hands off. I'd say I drove a solid share of the build, though it was a real team effort.", "my_share_percent": 30}
